target_customer: Pulmonology practices and health systems that pay for remote monitoring of lung disease patients (originally consumers buying a breath tracker)
problem: Clinicians cannot see how chronic lung patients breathe between visits, so exacerbations are caught late.
business_model: B2B remote patient monitoring device plus clinical monitoring service, reimbursed per patient
product_category: Wearable respiratory sensing and remote patient monitoring

founders.name: Neema Moraveji
education: Stanford, PhD (augmented self regulation, Calming Technology Lab)
founders.background_notes: YC page states a Stanford PhD; TechXplore 2014 describes the Calming Technology Lab.

founders.name: Jonathan Palley
founders.background_notes: Named with Moraveji as creator in 2014 press coverage; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom breath sensor hardware, algorithms and later FDA clearance in 2020 required hardware and regulatory work.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary respiration sensing and later FDA clearance, with a clinical monitoring service, raised copying costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; Wellinks, a COPD management company, acquired it in September 2024.

market_need_then: Consumer wearables in 2014 counted steps; the founders pitched breath tracking for stress and focus, later finding clinical demand in chronic lung disease.

identity.visual_style: Stone shaped clip on device that drew press attention for its look
identity.voice_and_tone: Calm and wellness oriented in 2014 consumer coverage

branding.brand_signature: The Spire Stone pebble shaped breath tracker

rebrands.why: Wikipedia mirror says the company became Spire Health; date and reason not found

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, Smithsonian and device reviews in 2014 and 2015 for the Stone

brand_strength.rationale: Consumer product earned wide press at launch but the consumer line was discontinued in 2019.

pivots.from: Consumer breath and stress tracker (Spire Stone)
pivots.to: B2B remote patient monitoring for lung disease
pivots.why: Wikipedia mirror says all direct to consumer products were discontinued in June 2019, support ending June 2020.

outcome_analysis: Spire launched a consumer breath tracker in 2014, pivoted in 2019 to clinical remote monitoring, won FDA clearance in 2020, raised 38 million dollars in 2021 and was acquired by Wellinks in September 2024 for an undisclosed non cash deal. Returns for investors are unknown.
notes: spirehealth.com returned 503. CB Insights lists a 9.97M Series B in April 2020 seen only in one aggregator, not recorded. Total raised estimates conflict (48.1M to 63M). 2021 round stage not stated by sources, so labeled other. No dated competitor sources found; press framed it against generic activity trackers. Palley founder status from press and a Wikipedia mirror, not the YC page. Deal terms undisclosed.
